comparison: Both evaluate competition experiments for ARID3B and KLF4 (C33, C34). OpenEval finds the differential competition patterns well-controlled and logically sound. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting additional negative controls (both methylated and unmethylated competitor DNA together) to validate the mechanistic interpretation.

Both assess ChIP-bisulfite sequencing data for in vivo validation (C52-C58). OpenEval considers this gold-standard evidence with strong statistical support. Peer reviewers explicitly state the manuscript 'was not successful in convincing us of the physiological relevance' and request ChIP-qPCR data due to poor quality/presentation of ChIP-seq data, directly challenging these claims.

Both evaluate mutagenesis experiments for KLF4 mechanistic characterization (C38-C43). OpenEval finds the systematic mutagenesis provides strong mechanistic evidence with clear decoupling of binding activities. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting more detailed domain dissection to identify which specific zinc finger mediates unmethylated DNA binding.

Both assess luciferase functional validation experiments (C44-C49). OpenEval finds strong support from dose-dependence, methylation-dependence, and differential mutant effects. Peer reviewers also support these claims, raising no concerns about the functional validation data in heterologous cells.

Both evaluate EMSA validation of microarray results (C23-C25) and false positive/negative rates (C65-C66). OpenEval considers the 73% validation rate reasonable with appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, explicitly requesting estimations about false positive/negative hits and questioning the overall reliability of the screening.

Both evaluate comparison with prior work and overlap with previous studies (C70-C71). OpenEval finds the partial overlap expected and appropriate given different methodologies. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting better discussion of overlap, discrepancies, and novelties, and specifically asking why Rfx proteins were not identified.

Both assess KD measurements using OIRD (C35-C37). OpenEval finds the nanomolar KD values with appropriate benchmarking to MBD2b provide strong quantitative support. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting more comprehensive biochemical characterization and comparison to published meCpG-protein affinities to validate physiological relevance.

Both evaluate dual-specificity findings with EMSA validation (C30-C32). OpenEval finds the integration of PDI dataset with EMSA validation appropriate and convincing. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about the broader biochemical characterization, requesting more comprehensive KD determinations and comparisons to published values.

Both evaluate the systematic screen methodology and prevalence claims (C2, C14, C22, C59, C73). OpenEval finds strong evidence from well-described experimental design with appropriate controls and statistical analysis. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting more detailed discussion of the protein microarray approach and estimations of false positive/negative rates.

Both address false positive/negative rates and method limitations (C65-C66). OpenEval appreciates the honest assessment and empirical validation data. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, explicitly requesting estimations about false positive/negative hits, indicating concern about screening reliability.

Both evaluate novel protein identifications including ZNF114/ZNF416 (C72). OpenEval considers these significant contributions to the field. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, specifically asking why ZNF114 and ZNF416 were not identified in previous screenings, indicating skepticism requiring better contextualization.

OpenEval evaluates enrichment analysis with statistical significance (C20-C21) and finds it appropriate with biological relevance supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific enrichment claims.

OpenEval evaluates functional validation in cells showing transcriptional consequences (C26-C27) with dose-dependence and methylation-dependence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific functional validation claims.

OpenEval evaluates contextualization and limitation acknowledgments (C59-C64, C68), finding appropriate discussion of screen comprehensiveness and saturation analysis. Peer review R1 touches on C59 but focuses on methodology rather than limitation discussion.

OpenEval evaluates background/context claims about established understanding in the field (C1, C7-C10). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background claims.

OpenEval evaluates broader implications and 'fifth alphabet' conceptual framework (C74-C77) as largely speculative despite supporting data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these interpretive/conceptual claims.
